# Narrow cubic terminal-rounding controls

Sixteen original closed cubic arches are generated by
`tools/svg_cubic_rounding_fixture.py`. Widths 1/3, heights 4/12, and independent
0/1⁄16 x/y phases exercise exact half-lattice coordinates without corpus artwork.
The source package uses the existing original SVG fixture generator, python-docx
(MIT), lxml (BSD) and standard-library packaging; no font programs are included.

`native-api.json` is a separate Windows GDI+ `GraphicsPath.Flatten` reference with
explicit flatness 0.25 and quantized input. Capture it with
`tools/capture-cubic-flatten-sweep.ps1 -QuantizeInput`. It is not a native reference.

The native reference inline-range capture is `capture.emf`; `capture.json`
binds source/capture hashes and confirms read-only, unchanged source state.
Open and confirm an owned scratch copy through the reference-application helper before calling
`tools/capture-svg-opacity-metafile.ps1`. The recorder
`tools/record_svg_group_cubic.py --fixture svg-cubic-terminal-rounding` extracts
its sixteen native PNG layers and records hashes, dimensions and origins.

Current subdivision matches all sixteen API contours and all sixteen browser-
decoded native RGBA layers exactly. Changing exact terminal half ties to even
breaks every native reference layer, producing 40 differing alpha pixels. This is a
counterexample to a global tie-rule change, not a new renderer implementation.
The browser regression includes editing/export/reopen, untouched package
preservation and byte-exact undo. The API/unit check is separately labeled.

Reproduce the isolated browser comparison with
`node tools/probe-svg-cubic-terminal-rounding.mjs OUTPUT.json` while shared Vite
is available on port 5173. `tools/probe_svg_cubic_terminal_precision.py` compares
13 arithmetic hypotheses against this family and the existing 113-case API
sweep; it records subdivision-budget errors instead of suppressing them.
